subject: Private VPC postcall recap — AcmeHealth regulatory & networking constraints
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acmehealth.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Private VPC postcall recap — AcmeHealth regulatory & networking constraints

Hi Alex & Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — helpful to get clarity on the regulatory and networking constraints driving your Private/VPC evaluation. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps. Please correct anything I mis-captured.

What we heard (pain points & drivers)
- Data residency & PHI: All inference for the pilot must run within a US-only VPC and be segmented so that logs and artifacts do not leave the customer environment.
- Air-gap / restricted egress: Some teams require no internet egress from the VPC; any external calls must be via an approved proxy or private peering.
- Key management: Customer-managed KMS keys required for model keys and auditability.
- Network constraints: No public endpoints; preference for AWS PrivateLink or Direct Connect/Transit Gateway peering.
- Latency & throughput goals: 95th percentile latency under ~200ms for chat workloads; sustained throughput of ~150 concurrent users during peak.

Goals & success criteria for POC
- Deploy Redwood Private (VPC) in a test account with your network team controlling VPC/subnets.
- Validate PHI handling, KMS integration, and audit logs.
- Run a 2-week load window to confirm latency/throughput and cost profile.

Immediate next steps
1) Camila: share SOC2 summary, network diagram template, and our Private VPC PoC checklist (attached).
2) Dev Patel (cc): schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/networking engineers — propose 60–90 min session to map ports/peering and KMS flows.
3) Alex/Priya: confirm whether a proxy-based egress model (approved proxy host) or private peering is preferable for your security team.
4) Marissa: loop in procurement for MSA/POC paperwork and any security addenda.

Attachments included:
- acmehealth_network_diagram.pdf (network diagram template)
- redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (SOC2 summary for review)
- private_vpc_poc_checklist.xlsx (PoC checklist)

Proposed deep-dive times (PST): Thu 1/21 10:00–11:30, Thu 1/21 14:00–15:30, Fri 1/22 09:00–10:30. Let me know what works.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Camila — this looks right. A couple clarifications from our side:
- For the pilot we will need KMS in our account and key policies that restrict usage to the Redwood nodes in our VPC; we can provide the exact ARNs during the deep-dive.
- Proxy vs peering: security prefers private peering for production, proxy for pilot if it significantly reduces setup time, but proxy must be go/no-go cleared by our security team.
- Procurement: we have an expedited POC budget, but we will need a brief scope doc for procurement (POC duration, expected spend cap).

Can you include an example scope/estimate in the materials? Also please add a short note about how audit logs (access and admin traces) are handled in Redwood Private.

Alex

Subject: Re: Private VPC postcall recap — AcmeHealth regulatory & networking constraints

Alex — great questions. Short answers and attachments below; full technical deep-dive will cover details.

- KMS: We support customer-managed KMS keys in your AWS account. Redwood Private components can be configured to use your CMKs; key ARNs and policies are applied via our deployment templates. Will review exact principal ARNs in the deep-dive.
- Proxy vs peering: For the POC we can support both models. Private peering (PrivateLink/Direct Connect) is our recommended approach for production. For the pilot we can stand up a proxy-based model if your security team signs off; we will document the proxy host and allowed egress rules.
- Audit logs: Redwood Private exposes admin and access logs that can be pushed to your S3/Kinesis or retained behind your logging stack. We also support forwarding to your SIEM via PrivateLink.

I've attached the SOC2 summary and the network diagram template. Also added a one-page scope/estimate for the POC (high-level):
- 8-week pilot, 2-week load validation
- estimated infra and license budget: $XXk–$YYk (will refine after sizing)
- success criteria: PHI-only processing inside VPC, KMS integration validated, latency & throughput targets met

Next steps
- Dev Patel: can you confirm availability for the deep-dive on Thu 1/21 at 14:00 PST (we'll treat that as tentative until we hear back)?
- Alex/Priya: I'll share the Drive folder (link below) with the attachments and scope doc.

Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/AcmeHealth/PrivateVPC/NetworkSpecs

Attachments: acmehealth_network_diagram.pdf, redwood_soc2_summary.pdf, private_vpc_poc_checklist.xlsx

If that looks good I'll schedule the deep-dive and loop in our infra lead for the technical session.

Thanks,
Camila
